$about: 2026-08-06, later the same day: recording a fix that shipped in PR #25 and was not written down at the time. Catching that omission is the reason the run-ordering guard in this change exists - a fix nobody records is indistinguishable from a fix nobody made.

$elicitation.$why: This corpus measures whether the tooling conforms - gates, manifests, drift counts. No person was prompted in any of these runs and none was meant to be, so it evidences nothing about whether the standard asks anybody anything. It was never labelled that way, which is how 377 green observations came to read as validation of a product whose central promise is being guided.

observations.evidence: standard/.gitattributes now ships, forcing `text eol=lf` on *.sh, *.mjs, .claude/hooks/* and scripts/spec/*. Verified with git's own resolver rather than by inspection: `git check-attr text eol -- standard/.claude/hooks/lib.sh` reports `text: set` and `eol: lf`, same for standard/scripts/spec/common.sh and standard/scripts/self-verify.mjs. The file is registered in standard.manifest.json as a required core entry (rule R19, adapt: merge), so a repo that loses it reports drift rather than silently reverting to the broken state - confirmed by `cd standard && node scripts/self-verify.mjs --skeleton`, which lists `.gitattributes` as PASS and reports drift 0 (70/70). The failure this closes: on a checkout with eol=crlf all ten shipped .sh guards exited 127 with empty stdout, so a hook whose only job is to deny a dangerous command neither denied nor complained.
